decision: Wrote a topic-plan change and no product code
why: The request is analysis plus an OpenSpec plan. No bundled playbook both forbids a PR and asks for these files.

decision: Chose a saved notebook plan over cards or a daily path
why: Cards and a daily mix need modules first. Chat can already draft cards when the user writes the prompt.
The archived assistant change already excludes shell execution, and a lab is a different product from review.

decision: Kept URL reuse inside the plan action
why: File dedup is a byte hash. A unique URL index would change the library dialog.

decision: Left the deck-empty home redirect unchanged
why: Bootstrap loads decks, not notebooks. The plan opens the notebook instead of Home.

decision: Strict OpenSpec validation passed for the change and for --all
why: The planning predicate is a valid change, not a product build.

decision: A later save does not rename the notebook
why: The user can rename a notebook after the first save. Overwriting that title would fight the existing notebook title editor.

decision: Drop dead draft URLs before the user sees them
why: The operator asked for HEAD then GET through the existing SSRF-guarded fetch. A dead suggestion is not a source.

decision: The plan starts in the existing assistant
why: The owner dropped the welcome dialog. A read-tool card can be changed by a later message. Apply creates the notebook and ingests page text through the existing URL ingest. No new table.
result: proposal, design, spec, and tasks revised before code
